mission.subtitle: Why this matters
paragraphs: Advanced AI systems are being deployed faster than our understanding of how to make them safe, predictable, and accountable. This raises questions: how do we ensure an autonomous system will behave as intended? How do we prevent bad actors from using them for harm?
AI Safety & Governance is a student society at Western. We discuss the risks posed by advanced AI, and foster a community at Western capable of engaging with this problem across disciplines.

fellowship.title: Launch your AI safety career with our fellowship
fellowship.body: Our 8-week introductory fellowship leads small groups through an interdisciplinary course covering how AI works, why it misbehaves, and what can be done about it through technical research and governance.

network.title: University Group Network
network.body: AISW is a part of an informal network of student AI safety groups at universities from Harvard to Hong Kong, financially supported by Kairos through the [Pathfinder Fellowship](https://pathfinder.kairos-project.org/).

alumni.title: Western Alumni & Faculty in AI Safety
alumni.subtitle: From Western to the frontier of making AI safe.

people.name: Sam Ramadori
people.now: Sam serves as the Co-President and Executive Director of LawZero, a nonprofit AI safety research organization he leads alongside Turing Award winner Yoshua Bengio. In this role, he oversees the organization's strategic, operational, and development efforts toward creating "safe-by-design" foundational AI systems that prioritize truthfulness, accountability, and public good. Additionally, he serves as an Ivey AI Fellow at Western University's Ivey Business School and works as an executive consultant in the climate and AI technology sectors.

people.name: Atrisha Sarkar
people.atWestern: Assistant Professor, Dept. of Electrical and Computer Engineering
people.now: Today, Dr. Sarkar serves as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Western University, where her research focuses on multiagent systems, behavioral game theory, and computational methods for human-centric AI safety. In the broader AI landscape, she investigates both individual and societal-level AI impacts—addressing safety challenges in autonomous vehicles, human-AI interaction dynamics, and online polarization. Beyond her core engineering appointment, she actively contributes to interdisciplinary AI governance and ethics as a Faculty Affiliate at the Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society, a member of Western's Rotman Institute of Philosophy, and a member of the Computational Institutional Science Lab.

people.name: Ashyana-Jasmine Kachra
people.atWestern: B.A. - Honours Specialization in Political Science
people.now: Ashyana-Jasmine currently serves as the Harmful Manipulation Lead at Google DeepMind in London, UK. In this role, she focuses on frontier risks, specifically researching and evaluating AI models to mitigate deceptive behaviors and prevent artificial intelligence from being misused to manipulate human thoughts and beliefs. Prior to taking on this lead position, she served as an AI Ethics & Safety Manager at Google DeepMind.

join.statSub: Help us change that by launching your safety career.
paragraphs: Our 8-week fellowship introduces small groups of undergrad and grad students to interdisciplinary perspectives on AI risk. You’ll learn the perspectives of scientists dissecting AI brains, US-China AI policymakers, leading philosophers, and more.
Fellows also receive career guidance, and advice on how to apply to the 200+ AI safety fellowships, graduate programs, and internships that help new grads break into an impactful career.

pillars.title: Technical
pillars.body: Understanding how modern AI systems work, where they fail, and what makes them difficult to align, interpret, and evaluate.

pillars.title: Policy & Governance
pillars.body: Examining the institutions, regulations, and international frameworks needed to manage the deployment of increasingly capable systems.

pillars.title: Philosophy & Ethics
pillars.body: Asking what 'safe' and 'aligned' actually mean: questions of value, uncertainty, and responsibility that technical work alone cannot answer.

footer.disclaimer: AI Safety & Governance is a student society and is not officially affiliated with Western University.
